beats.narration_slice: Outside pressure is lower at high altitude.
beats.visual: Full-bleed crayon illustration from outside a passenger airplane cruising high above a thick cloud layer, with the aircraft surrounded by thin, sparse-looking high-altitude atmosphere and expansive cool blue sky; no text, labels, borders, panels or inset framing, with the bottom 8-10% kept naturally calm for subtitles.
beats.purpose: show that the airplane is flying in a lower-pressure high-altitude environment
beats.visual_fingerprint: exterior wide aerial view of a passenger jet above clouds, cool blue daylight, sparse atmospheric strokes around the fuselage, airplane placed diagonally in the upper half with open sky below
beats.continuity: establishes the high-altitude exterior before moving inside the pressurized cabin

beats.narration_slice: A break lets cabin air rush out.
beats.visual: Inside the aircraft cabin in full-bleed crayon style, a damaged side window is seen from a close three-quarter angle as loose lightweight objects and dense directional crayon airflow strokes stream outward through the opening; passengers remain safely farther back, with no readable text or enclosing frame.
beats.purpose: show cabin air escaping through a broken window
beats.visual_fingerprint: close three-quarter cabin view centered on one broken window, warm orange hazard accents at the opening, loose paper and fabric pulled outward, strong horizontal airflow strokes exiting toward open sky
beats.continuity: moves from the high-altitude exterior into the cabin where the pressure difference creates outward airflow

beats.narration_slice: Airflow is strongest near the opening.
beats.visual: A tight side-on crayon view of the broken window zone shows the most concentrated, fastest-looking airflow strokes packed immediately beside the opening, with nearby lightweight objects sharply angled toward it and calmer cabin space visible beyond; no labels or printed arrows.
beats.purpose: show that the strongest airflow is localized close to the broken opening
beats.visual_fingerprint: tight side profile of window and adjacent seat row, dense converging wax-crayon streaks nearest the opening, nearby scarf and loose items strongly deflected, focal hazard occupying the upper-right of the vertical frame
beats.continuity: focuses tightly on the same physical cause while isolating the high-speed zone nearest the opening

beats.narration_slice: Farther away, the air may move much less.
beats.visual: A wide view from the opposite end of the same cabin shows the broken window small in the distant background while foreground passengers, seat fabric and loose objects remain comparatively still; the Newton-Inspired Scholar stands securely in the calm foreground indicating the contrast through posture only, without signs or text.
beats.purpose: contrast the strong airflow near the opening with much weaker air movement farther away
beats.visual_fingerprint: wide rear-cabin perspective with calm foreground and distant broken window, host positioned low-left beside nearly still seatbacks, airflow marks confined mainly to the far background, strong depth separation
beats.continuity: pulls far back from the opening to reveal how rapidly the airflow effect diminishes with distance

beats.visual: A medium frontal cabin shot shows a seated passenger reacting to the pressure drop with a strained breathing posture while the surrounding cabin gains subtle thinning, expanding crayon atmosphere strokes and cooler tones; the broken window is out of frame so the focus stays on the consequence, with no labels or medical text.
beats.purpose: show the breathing difficulty caused by falling cabin pressure
beats.visual_fingerprint: medium frontal passenger portrait in a different cabin row, hands near chest and visibly labored posture, cool diffused cabin light, sparse expanding atmospheric strokes around face and shoulders, centered composition
beats.continuity: shifts from airflow location to the human consequence of the cabin pressure dropping

beats.narration_slice: Oxygen masks may drop as pilots descend.
beats.visual: Full-bleed upward-angled cabin view with several oxygen masks freshly hanging from the overhead units as passengers reach for them, while through the windows the airplane is visibly descending toward a lower cloud layer and warmer atmosphere; the Newton-Inspired Scholar is seated and correctly using a mask, with no printed instructions.
beats.purpose: show oxygen masks deploying while the aircraft descends toward safer altitude
beats.visual_fingerprint: low upward camera angle emphasizing dangling oxygen masks overhead, passengers reaching upward, host seated at lower-right wearing a mask, slanted horizon and rising cloud layer outside indicating descent
beats.continuity: follows the breathing problem with the immediate cabin safety response and descent

beats.narration_slice: That sudden pressure loss is called rapid decompression.
beats.visual: A final full-bleed crayon cabin scene freezes the overall event into one clear visual: the broken window glows with restrained warm hazard accents, concentrated airflow remains localized near it, oxygen masks hang farther inside, and the aircraft is now lower above a thicker cloud layer outside; no labels, text, borders, cards or footer.
beats.purpose: visually summarize the sudden cabin pressure-loss event described as rapid decompression
beats.visual_fingerprint: wide diagonal cabin tableau combining distant broken window, localized airflow, hanging masks and visibly lower-altitude clouds outside, warm-to-cool spatial gradient with a calm subtitle-safe lower edge
beats.continuity: resolves the sequence by showing the airflow, pressure-loss response and descent together in one final in-world summary
